title: CNCF Research Shows Virtual Machines Remain Central as AI Workloads Evolve
gist: A CNCF/Linux Foundation Research survey of 492 practitioners (Sept 2026, sponsored by CNCF and Broadcom) finds VMs still host an average 53% of production apps; rather than being displaced by containers, VMs are seeing fresh demand from AI/agentic workloads that need stronger isolation, with MicroVM sandboxing and confidential computing adoption set to rise.

insights.claim: A CNCF and Linux Foundation Research survey of 492 cloud-native practitioners (September 2026) found that virtual machines host an average of 53% of production applications despite widespread Kubernetes adoption.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: The virtualisation layer remains a durable revenue pool; the 'containers kill VMs' narrative is overstated.

insights.claim: Large enterprises lean more heavily on VMs: organisations with over 10,000 employees run an average of 64% of production apps on VMs, versus 45% at organisations with fewer than 500 employees; 51% of all respondents run at least half their production apps on VMs.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: VM-centric vendors' exposure skews to large enterprise accounts, where migration away is slowest.
insights.locator: The survey found that 51% of respondents

insights.claim: 71% of respondents who gave current and expected figures expect their VM share of workloads to stay within the same range over the next year, pointing to coexistence rather than wholesale migration to containers.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Expect stable, not declining, VM demand near-term — supportive for virtualisation licensing incumbents.

insights.claim: Cloud-native adoption does not necessarily mean moving away from VMs: containers bring portability and packaging efficiency, while VMs keep offering isolation and support for workloads tied to dedicated operating systems.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Hybrid VM+container platforms, not pure-container plays, match how enterprises actually run production.
insights.quote: The research challenges the assumption that cloud-native adoption necessarily means moving away from virtual machines.

insights.claim: Among organisations expanding their VM footprint, 47% cite security and isolation and 34% specifically cite AI and agentic workloads as contributing factors.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: AI agents are a new demand driver for virtualisation/isolation infrastructure — a second-order beneficiary of agentic AI.
insights.locator: Among organisations expanding their VM footprint, 47%

insights.claim: Because AI agents generate and execute code and access external systems, running that code beside sensitive data or shared infrastructure creates new risk, and VMs offer a stronger boundary than containers that share the host kernel.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Agent sandboxing is becoming a must-have infrastructure layer; watch hardware-isolation and MicroVM vendors.
insights.locator: AI agents increasingly generate and execute code

insights.claim: Organisations are containing AI workloads via hardware-level VM isolation, containers running inside VMs, and MicroVM sandboxing.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Three distinct isolation patterns map to different vendor categories to track.
insights.locator: Virtual machines offer a stronger isolation boundary

insights.claim: MicroVM sandboxing adoption is planned to grow from 20% current use to 30%, and confidential computing from 12% to 26%, though these are stated intentions rather than confirmed deployments.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Confidential computing roughly doubling in intent is a notable tailwind for TEE-capable silicon and cloud offerings — discount for survey optimism.
insights.locator: The survey also points to growing interest

insights.claim: 8% of VM-using respondents run KubeVirt, the CNCF project that manages virtual machines through Kubernetes resources and APIs, bringing VM lifecycle into Kubernetes operations.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: KubeVirt is still early (single-digit adoption) — a gauge for how fast Kubernetes displaces traditional hypervisor management planes.
insights.locator: Kubernetes is also beginning to play a role

insights.claim: 61% of respondents describe their VM and container admin teams as collaborative or fully integrated, making mixed-workload management a shared platform-engineering responsibility.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Buyers increasingly want unified platforms spanning VMs and containers.

insights.claim: The survey was sponsored by CNCF and Broadcom, so its findings reflect reported industry perspectives rather than a full census of cloud-native deployments.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Broadcom (VMware owner) co-sponsoring a 'VMs remain central' study is a bias flag worth weighting.
insights.locator: The survey was sponsored by CNCF and Broadcom
